acceptance_signals: DEVELOPMENT_PLAN records one clearly bounded future README product-entry refactor and documentation-responsibility split.
The backlog item classifies README content as Product, Reference, Architecture, or Evidence before migration and forbids moving the existing monolith into another monolithic document.
The backlog acceptance model prioritizes a new reader answering six core product and usage questions within two to three minutes rather than enforcing a hard line-count target.
The backlog preserves unique evidence, release-channel distinctions, and source-of-truth ownership while reducing primary calls to action and architecture duplication.
STATUS and the dated development log state that the item is recorded but not started, scheduled, admitted for implementation, or granted downstream authority.
Relevant documentation, task governance, repository governance, scope, privacy, and diff checks pass.

decision.rationale: The accountable human reviewed structured proposal prp-b61ca3d6797c4cdcb51c4002617bc0b2 and admitted that exact task through an explicit admission control.

requirement.summary: Record the reviewed README product-entry refactor and documentation-responsibility split as a future product backlog item, including responsibility classification before migration, release-channel clarity, three primary calls to action, one README architecture diagram, preservation of unique evidence, and reader-centered acceptance signals, without starting or implementing the refactor.

items: A backlog record could be mistaken for authorization to rewrite README.
Duplicating detailed content across planning and status surfaces could create new source-of-truth drift.
A hard size target could incentivize deletion of important release, authority, or evidence boundaries.
Creating a new CLI reference without classifying existing content could merely relocate the current monolith.
Reviewed assumption: DEVELOPMENT_PLAN owns strategic priority and acceptance boundaries for the future item.
Reviewed assumption: STATUS owns the current fact that the item is recorded but not started.
Reviewed assumption: The existing 2026-08-21 dated log is the appropriate append-only session evidence surface.
Reviewed assumption: README itself should remain unchanged until a separately admitted implementation task exists.
Reviewed unknown: The future implementation date and priority relative to other product work are not decided.
Reviewed unknown: Whether any new compact CLI index is needed remains subject to the later section-by-section responsibility inventory.
Reviewed unknown: Real unbriefed-reader comprehension requires future human evidence and cannot be proved by static documentation tests.

title: Record README product-entry refactor as a bounded backlog item
